Security artifacts and SOC2/KMS talking points
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~90 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (AE), Priya Patel (SE), Samir Diaz (Sales), Jordan Lee (Sales Ops)

[00:00] Alex: Okay everyone, thanks for joining — we'll run an hour and a half, quick enablement on messaging and then demo practice and roleplay. Priya, do you want to kick us off with the one-liner?
[00:23] Priya: Yeah sure, so our one-liner is: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM serving predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
[00:35] Samir: Quick note — sales folks prefer a shorter one: "High-performance LLM inference with predictable latency and lower unit cost".
[00:45] Priya: Right, we can alternate that depending on whether it's technical or exec audience.
[00:52] Alex: Walk through the pillars briefly. Priya — runtime features?
[01:05] Priya: Runtime: GPU-optimized inference, continuous batching, KV cache prefix caching, optimized kernels, and automatic routing by policy. Emphasize that we do smart routing — like region/cost/latency rules — and automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
[01:28] Samir: Sometimes customers ask about the KV thing, they hear "K V cache" and get lost. Maybe a one-line definition: "KV cache is the model's token cache used to speed incremental decoding".
[01:40] Priya: Good call. Add that to script.
[01:45] Jordan: Competitor framing — what's the shortest differentiator vs Anthropic/OpenAI?
[01:52] Alex: Say: "We are production-first: better observability, cost controls, and unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." Keep it short.
[02:05] Priya: Also mention our Optimize toolkit — batching, quantization recs, and quality monitors tied to evals, that resonates with platform teams who run many prompts.
[02:20] Samir: Walkthrough of typical objections list?
[02:25] Alex: Yes: 1) Latency vs cost — customers want sub-100ms but care about unit cost on high QPS. 2) Dedicated vs hosted — data isolation and predictable throughput. 3) Security/compliance — SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, and VPC/on-prem. 4) Model regressions — tie to evals and rollouts.
[02:55] Priya: We'll run three roleplays: (A) Technical buyer worried about latency; (B) Security/compliance buyer; (C) Economic buyer focused on unit cost. Then demo practice.
[03:10] Alex: Alright Samir, you'll be roleplaying the latency buyer first. Priya, you're SE.

--- Roleplay A (Latency buyer) ---
[03:30] Samir (buyer): We need sub-100ms p95 for chat, our app tight on latency. How do you get there?
[03:40] Priya (SE): Great question. We hit low latency through optimized kernels, continuous batching that respects SLOs, and KV/prefix caching so repeat context is fast. For edge cases we have Dedicated pools with pinned GPUs and autoscaling policies.
[03:58] Samir: What about cold start and token overhead?
[04:02] Priya: We mitigate with warm pools and configurable idle timeouts; you can reserve capacity for hot routes. Also model choice matters — smaller distill or quantized variants trade quality for latency.
[04:18] Samir: And fallback?
[04:20] Priya: Smart routing can fallback to an L2 model or different region if capacity's constrained; we also support multi-model rollouts.
[04:30] Samir: Great.

--- Roleplay B (Security/compliance buyer) ---
[04:45] Alex (buyer): We're in finance, need SOC 2, encryption at rest, and control over keys. Can you do HSM/KMS?
[04:56] Priya: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, RBAC and SSO/SAML for identity, and provide audit logs and data residency options with Private deployments. For the most sensitive workloads, Private on-prem or VPC with customer-managed control plane.
[05:20] Alex: How is data retained?
[05:23] Priya: We surface retention policies at route-level; by default hosted doesn't persist training data, but Dedicated/Private can be configured per contract. We'll follow up with the security one-pager.
[05:36] Alex (AE): Jordan, remind them we need to share SOC2 link and encryption spec after the call.
[05:40] Jordan: Yep, added as action item.

--- Roleplay C (Economic buyer) ---
[05:50] Samir (buyer): Your price looks higher than OpenAI for large models. Why pay Redwood?
[05:58] Priya: We help reduce unit cost through batching, caching, quantization recommendations, and smart routing to cheaper model variants. Also our Dedicated offering provides predictable throughput so you don't overprovision and pay for idle GPUs. The total cost of ownership often comes down once you account for dev ops and SLO overhead.
[06:18] Samir: Customers ask for examples — can we give a quick benchmark?
[06:22] Alex: Yes, use the model catalog benchmark: e.g., for 1k QPS with 16 token avg, dedicated with batching can reduce per-token cost by ~30% vs naive hosted. (Note: numbers vary by workload.)

[06:40] Priya: Demo prep — I'll share the runbook: start with brief one-liner, then architecture slide, then live demo showing latency dashboard, token-level cost breakdown, and a model swap fallback.
[06:55] Samir: For demo timing, keep live portion to 8-10 minutes, otherwise execs drop off.
[07:05] Priya: Agreed. We'll keep the deep trace and KV cache visible but optional in the appendix.

--- Live demo practice (mock app) ---
[07:20] Priya: Starting demo: show console, route config with autoscaling policy, choose a hosted model, stream a response. (typing noise)
[07:45] System: [demo - streaming started]
[07:52] Priya: Note the per-token cost column on the right — this is where you show unit economics.
[08:05] Samir: Interrupt: accidentally clicked 'Dedicated' in UI during demo — good learning: slow clicks look like bugs.
[08:12] Alex: Good note. Practice the "if click misfires" recovery line: "That's our dedicated preview; let's switch back to hosted for the flow."
[08:25] Priya: Also practice the quantization slide: "We recommend int8/int4 options with quality checks for high-throughput workloads."

[08:40] Samir: Question: how deep do we go on kernel/compilation stuff with infra teams?
[08:46] Priya: With infra/K8s teams go deeper — talk about kernel selection, sequence length distributions, and our GPU-optimized runtime. With product managers keep it higher level.

[09:00] Jordan: Some transcription glitches to watch for on recorded demos — Fireflies often mislabels "KV" as "K V" and "Redwood Dedicated" as "Redwood Dedicate" in notes.
[09:12] Alex: Ha, yeah we should add a note for enablement doc.

[09:20] Priya: Let's run a second round with Alex taking the security buyer. Focus on artifacts to send post-call.
[09:30] Alex (buyer): What's your SLA for Dedicated?
[09:34] Priya: SLA is typically 99.9% uptime and latency targets per contract; specifics vary by region and capacity commit. We can push exact SLO numbers based on the customer's commit tier.
[09:50] Alex: Good.

[10:00] (Discussion continues—red team feedback, slide edits, callouts)

[45:00] Priya: Quick mid-call recap — action items: add KV cache sentence to script, add latency vs cost slide, and attach SOC2 link.

[60:00] Alex: Let's time the demo again — Priya, you have 10 minutes to run the streaming demo and show a model swap fallback. Samir will interject as buyer.
[60:12] Priya: Starting streaming demo...
[68:30] Samir: Noticed trailing latency during the second request — is that due to cold start?
[68:36] Priya: Probably. Explain warm pools and reserve capacity; show how to configure idle timeouts in the route.

[80:00] Alex: Wrap-up — what's the final pitch?
[80:05] Priya: "Redwood is the inference platform that lets engineers ship low-latency, cost-effective LLM features across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with first-class observability and operational controls."
[80:20] Samir: Solid.
[80:30] Alex: Any other items?
[80:33] Jordan: I'll share the recording and the security one-pager.
[80:36] Alex: Great. Last callouts: update the slide deck, add an appendix with kernel/compilation notes for SEs, and schedule the follow-up 30-minute roleplay.
[80:50] Priya: I'll own the appendix updates.
[81:00] Alex: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Notes and imperfections: transcription includes occasional word swaps and mis-hearings, names may be abbreviated in Fireflies export. References to benchmarks and example numbers were illustrative and must be validated before sharing with customers.
